title: Independence from Portugal Ends Five Centuries of Colonial Rule
description: On July 12, 1975, Sao Tome and Principe gained independence from Portugal in the wake of the Carnation Revolution, ending nearly five centuries of colonial rule built around cocoa and coffee plantations and slave labour. Manuel Pinto da Costa of the Movimento de Libertacao de Sao Tome e Principe became the first president, inheriting an economy almost entirely dependent on a small number of large estates known as rocas.

title: MLSTP Establishes One-Party Marxist-Leninist State
description: The MLSTP under Pinto da Costa proclaimed itself the sole legal political party at independence, establishing a one-party Marxist-Leninist state aligned with Angola, Cuba and the Soviet bloc. Political life was channelled through the party for the next fifteen years and dissent was suppressed, while the state took over the largest cocoa plantations.

title: Admission to the United Nations as Smallest African State
description: Sao Tome and Principe was admitted to the United Nations on September 16, 1975, as the smallest sovereign state in Africa by population. Membership anchored the new country's place in the non-aligned movement and gave it access to multilateral aid that would become a structural feature of its budget.

title: Nationalisation of Cocoa Plantations and Mass Portuguese Exodus
description: Within months of independence the new government nationalised the colonial-era cocoa and coffee plantations, while almost the entire Portuguese settler and managerial class left the islands. Cocoa production began a decades-long collapse from roughly 30,000 tonnes in the early 1970s to a few thousand tonnes, depriving the new state of its main export earner.

title: Alleged Coup Attempt and Angolan-Cuban Military Presence
description: Pinto da Costa announced an attempted coup in 1978 said to involve former interior minister Carlos da Graca and external backers, prompting the deployment of Angolan and Cuban troops to the islands as a presidential guard. The episode tightened MLSTP control and entrenched a security relationship with Luanda and Havana.

title: Purge of Prime Minister Miguel Trovoada
description: Prime Minister Miguel Trovoada, a co-founder of the MLSTP, was dismissed and later arrested in a power struggle with Pinto da Costa, accused of plotting against the regime. He was held without trial for two years before being released into exile, becoming the most prominent opponent of the one-party system.

title: Economic Liberalisation Pivots Away from Marxist Model
description: Faced with collapsing cocoa output and chronic foreign-exchange shortages, the MLSTP began a quiet economic liberalisation in the mid-1980s, courting Western donors and the World Bank and loosening state control over plantations. The shift prefigured the formal abandonment of Marxism-Leninism a few years later.

title: World Bank Structural Adjustment Programme
description: Sao Tome and Principe entered a structural adjustment programme with the World Bank and IMF in 1987, devaluing the dobra, lifting price controls and opening the door to private management of plantations. The programme stabilised the macroeconomy at the cost of unemployment and a steep rise in import prices.

title: Constitutional Amendment Introduces Multiparty Democracy
description: In 1990 a referendum approved a new constitution that ended the MLSTP monopoly and introduced multiparty democracy, semi-presidentialism and civil liberties. The reform put Sao Tome and Principe among the earliest African one-party states to liberalise, ahead of the wider continental wave of 1991-1993.

title: First Multiparty Elections and Peaceful Defeat of MLSTP
description: The January 1991 legislative elections were won decisively by the opposition Partido de Convergencia Democratica, and in March Miguel Trovoada was elected president unopposed after the MLSTP boycotted the runoff. The MLSTP became the first ruling Marxist party in Africa to surrender power peacefully through the ballot box.

title: Brief Bloodless Military Coup Against Trovoada
description: On August 15, 1995, junior officers led by Lieutenant Manuel Quintas de Almeida briefly seized power and detained President Trovoada, complaining about pay and conditions. Mediation by the Angolan and Portuguese governments restored constitutional rule within a week in exchange for an amnesty, an early sign of the chronic fragility of civil-military relations.

title: Trovoada Re-elected as Independent
description: Miguel Trovoada was re-elected to a second presidential term in July 1996, defeating MLSTP candidate Manuel Pinto da Costa in a runoff and consolidating the new multiparty system. The election confirmed the alternation pattern that would dominate the next three decades.

title: Diplomatic Recognition of Taiwan in Exchange for Aid
description: In May 1997 Sao Tome and Principe switched recognition from the People's Republic of China to the Republic of China on Taiwan, becoming one of a handful of African states to do so in exchange for development assistance. Taiwanese aid funded health, agriculture and a small embassy footprint over the following two decades.

title: Joint Development Zone Treaty with Nigeria
description: In February 2001 Sao Tome and Principe signed a treaty with Nigeria establishing a Joint Development Zone over disputed Gulf of Guinea waters, splitting hydrocarbon revenues 60-40 in Nigeria's favour. The deal formalised access to potentially significant offshore oil and triggered a wave of speculation about a future petro-state.

title: Election of Independent Businessman Fradique de Menezes
description: Fradique de Menezes, a cocoa exporter and political independent backed by the Acao Democratica Independente, won the July 2001 presidential election against Pinto da Costa. His victory marked the entry of business interests into the centre of national politics on the eve of the offshore oil rush.

title: Bloodless Coup Briefly Removes President de Menezes
description: On July 16, 2003, while President de Menezes was abroad in Nigeria, Major Fernando Pereira and a group of officers seized power complaining about corruption around the oil sector and conditions in the army. After a week of mediation by CPLP, Nigerian and US envoys, constitutional rule was restored under an amnesty deal that left no one prosecuted.

title: First Joint Development Zone Oil Licensing Round
description: Later in 2003 Sao Tome and Principe and Nigeria launched the first licensing round in the Joint Development Zone, awarding blocks to a consortium led by ChevronTexaco. Allegations of irregularities in the bidding became one of the recurring political controversies of the de Menezes era.

title: Prime Minister Maria das Neves Dismissed Over Corruption Allegations
description: In September 2004 President de Menezes dismissed Prime Minister Maria das Neves and her cabinet amid corruption allegations linked to humanitarian food aid and the oil sector, replacing her with Damiao Vaz d'Almeida. The episode foreshadowed a pattern of short-lived governments and parliamentary crises throughout the decade.

title: Petroleum Revenue Management Law Adopted
description: In late 2004 parliament adopted a Petroleum Revenue Management Law modelled on international best practice, creating a National Oil Account, a permanent fund and oversight bodies in anticipation of large offshore revenues. The law became a reference point for subsequent debates about transparency even as actual oil revenues remained negligible.

title: De Menezes Re-elected and Tofe Coalition Wins Legislatives
description: Fradique de Menezes was re-elected to a second term in July 2006, while the legislative elections produced a new coalition government under Tome Vera Cruz of the Movimento Democratico das Forcas da Mudanca. The configuration entrenched cohabitation between presidency and parliament that would persist through later cycles.

title: Patrice Trovoada Government Falls in Bia Mauricio Crisis
description: Patrice Trovoada, son of former president Miguel Trovoada and leader of ADI, formed a short-lived government in 2008 that was brought down within months by a no-confidence vote linked to the so-called Bia Mauricio affair over alleged irregular financing. The crisis underlined the fragility of parliamentary majorities in the multi-party system.

title: Currency Pegged to the Euro Under IMF Programme
description: In 2008 Sao Tome and Principe began a currency-board-style arrangement that culminated in formally pegging the dobra to the euro at a fixed rate, supported by Portugal and an IMF programme. The peg, implemented in 2010, was intended to anchor inflation in an economy where most goods are imported.

title: Alleged Coup Plot and Arrests of Former Officers
description: In February 2009 the government announced it had foiled a plot to overthrow President de Menezes involving former military officers and exiled politicians, leading to several arrests. The episode kept civil-military tensions on the agenda even as the country received praise for democratic stability.

title: Patrice Trovoada and ADI Win Legislative Elections
description: Patrice Trovoada led the Acao Democratica Independente to victory in the August 2010 legislative elections and returned as prime minister. The election began ADI's emergence as the dominant electoral force of the 2010s and 2020s, anchored in clientelist networks across the islands.

title: Manuel Pinto da Costa Returns as Elected President
description: In August 2011 the founding president Manuel Pinto da Costa returned to office at the age of 74, this time elected as an independent in a runoff against ADI's Evaristo Carvalho. His victory inaugurated an unusually tense period of cohabitation with Trovoada's government.

title: Trovoada Government Falls to No-Confidence Motion
description: In December 2012 Patrice Trovoada's ADI government lost a parliamentary no-confidence vote and was replaced by a four-party coalition under MLSTP's Gabriel Costa. The transition was orderly but reflected the chronic instability of governing majorities that had marked the country since 1991.

title: ADI Wins Absolute Majority in Legislative Elections
description: In October 2014 the ADI led by Patrice Trovoada won an absolute majority in the National Assembly, a first under the multiparty system, returning Trovoada as prime minister with a far stronger mandate. The result allowed a four-year period of single-party government.

title: Diplomatic Switch from Taiwan to People's Republic of China
description: In December 2016 Sao Tome and Principe abruptly broke diplomatic relations with Taiwan and re-established ties with the People's Republic of China, citing economic interests. The switch, negotiated by the Trovoada government, was framed in Taipei and Beijing as a significant diplomatic victory for the PRC in Africa.

title: Evaristo Carvalho Elected President with ADI Backing
description: In July 2016 Evaristo Carvalho, the candidate of the governing ADI, was declared elected president after Pinto da Costa withdrew from the second round alleging irregularities. The result completed ADI's grip on both presidency and government.

title: Coalition of MLSTP and Smaller Parties Ousts ADI
description: Legislative elections in October 2018 produced a hung parliament in which ADI lost its majority, and a coalition led by the MLSTP under Jorge Bom Jesus formed a new government. The shift returned the historic ruling party to office for the first time since 1999.

title: Cabinda-Style Oil Hopes Fade After Disappointing Drilling
description: By 2019 a series of disappointing exploration wells in the Joint Development Zone and Sao Tomean exclusive economic zone had largely dispelled hopes that the country would become a significant oil producer. Most international companies wound down operations, leaving the petroleum revenue framework largely unused.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Hits Tourism-Dependent Economy
description: Sao Tome and Principe recorded its first COVID-19 cases in April 2020 and imposed lockdowns and border closures that crushed the small but growing tourism sector. GDP contracted in 2020 and the government turned to IMF emergency financing to plug the budget hole.

title: Carlos Vila Nova Elected President
description: In September 2021 Carlos Vila Nova, the ADI candidate, won a runoff against Guilherme Posser da Costa of MLSTP to become the fifth elected president since 1991. His victory restored cohabitation with the MLSTP-led government and set the stage for the 2022 legislative reset.

title: ADI Returns to Power Under Patrice Trovoada
description: In September 2022 ADI won an absolute majority in the legislative elections, returning Patrice Trovoada to the prime ministership for a fourth time. The result reunited the executive under ADI control alongside President Vila Nova.

title: Alleged Coup Attempt and Custody Deaths in Sao Tome Barracks
description: In November 2022 the Trovoada government announced it had repelled an attempted coup at the army barracks in Sao Tome, with at least four detainees killed in custody in the immediate aftermath. The deaths drew sharp condemnation from rights groups and the United Nations and triggered prosecutions of senior officers.

title: Floods and Landslides in Sao Tome Capital
description: Heavy seasonal rains in late 2023 caused flooding and landslides in and around Sao Tome city, destroying homes and damaging infrastructure on the steep volcanic terrain. The episode underlined the country's growing exposure to extreme rainfall events linked to a warming Atlantic.

title: IMF Extended Credit Facility Programme Approved
description: The IMF approved a 40-month Extended Credit Facility for Sao Tome and Principe in October 2023 to support fiscal consolidation, defend the euro peg and clear domestic arrears. The programme reaffirmed multilateral creditors as the central anchor of macroeconomic policy.

title: Inflation Surge from Imported Food and Fuel Prices
description: Inflation rose into double digits in 2024 driven by global food and fuel prices passing through the euro peg, eroding real incomes in a country that imports almost all staples. The Trovoada government rolled out targeted social transfers and fuel subsidies to limit the political fallout.

title: New Submarine Cable Improves Internet Connectivity
description: A new submarine cable landed in Sao Tome in 2024, dramatically improving the small archipelago's international internet bandwidth and reducing reliance on a single legacy link. The project, supported by regional financiers, was framed as a precondition for any meaningful digital economy.

title: Cocoa Renaissance Gains Speciality Market Foothold
description: By 2024 a small group of producers had established Sao Tomean fine-flavour cocoa as a recognised origin in European speciality chocolate markets, with prices well above bulk West African levels. The revival was modest in volume but politically significant as a counterweight to the post-independence collapse of the plantation sector.

title: Constitutional Court Confirms Conviction in 2022 Barracks Deaths
description: In 2025 the courts confirmed convictions of senior military officers for their role in the deaths of detainees following the November 2022 alleged coup attempt, in proceedings closely watched by international observers. The judgements were one of the few cases in the region in which security force commanders were held accountable in court.

title: Renewable Energy Push and Hydropower Rehabilitation
description: Sao Tome and Principe expanded a programme of solar mini-grids and rehabilitated small hydropower plants in 2025 to reduce dependence on imported diesel for electricity. Donor financing from the African Development Bank and the European Union underpinned the rollout.
